thread:
Ajay: Quick proposal — shift most nightly GPU batch jobs to transient (interruptible) pools during off-peak (02:00–06:00 UTC). Goal: cut GPU costs ~30% and free reserved capacity for interactive. Thoughts? :chart_with_downwards_trend:
Marie: Sounds good in principle. What are we doing on evictions? Hard to have noisy requeues during morning business hours.
Ajay: Plan: require checkpointing for long jobs + a two-tier fallback: 1) immediate requeue to reserved pool if capacity available, 2) otherwise move to low-priority backfill queue that runs until next off-peak window. Also add rapid autoscale for short interactive bursts.
Sophie: Can we protect interactive/prompt infra with a higher priority class so they never get shoved by batch?
Ajay: Yes — interactive gets PriorityClass=high and an "interactive:true" tag. Batch gets priority low and tolerates eviction. Example job label changes:```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  labels:
    workload: nightly-batch
    transient: "true"
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checkpoint: "s3://redwood-checkpoints/{{job_id}}"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: trainer
        image: redwood/trainer:stable
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```
Dave: Two concerns: 1) data locality — some datasets live in eu-west and we shouldn't route jobs across regions (eggs on network egress). 2) burst autoscale could spike costs if not bounded.
Ajay: Agreed. We'll enforce nodeAffinity: region and a max-burst cap. Autoscaler config example (pseudocode):```json
{"max_burst_gpus": 50, "offpeak_window": "02:00-06:00 UTC", "fallback_policy": "reserved_then_backfill"}
```
Kevin: capacity-bot ran a dry run on test cluster — eviction rate for transient pool at 02:00 was 18% (mostly short <10m jobs), average requeue latency 22s. capacity-bot: results attached to #infra-playbooks.
capacity-bot: simulated cost drop ~28% after shifting 60% of batch jobs.
Marie: If eviction rate is that high, we need more aggressive checkpointing defaults. Maybe enforce checkpoint every 5m for any job >30m.
Sophie: SGTM. Also suggest we tag certain non-critical evals as "best-effort" so they go to the backfill queue automatically.
Ajay: Rollout plan: canary 10% of nightly-batch for 1 week -> evaluate evictions and requeue latency -> 50% for another week -> full roll. Ops playbook update + runbook for oncall. I'll own canary; @Marie can you update runbook + docs?
Marie: On it. I'll add churn alerts and a dashboard card for transient pool eviction rate + 95p requeue latency.
Dave: Add a small circuit-breaker: if reserved pool usage >85% during window, pause further transient-to-reserved requeues to avoid cascading pressure.
Ajay: Good call. We'll codify that in autoscaler.
Sophie: +1 :thumbsup:
Kevin: I'll schedule another dry run after the canary is configured. capacity-bot: will post metrics to #eng-infra during the canary.
Ajay: Thanks everyone — I'll post the canary config and TL;DR in this thread once it's live. :rocket:
